value.description: Close third person limited to the shepherd, past tense, with rain and weather carrying the emotional register; chapters end on definite beats of choice or discovery.

sample.reason: Chooses close-third past-tense narration and weather as emotional register.

card.identity: Elias's mother, forty-four, works mornings at the Halder County Co-op register. Her hands ache from arthritis; the clinic bill in Rockford is what keeps Elias's paycheck sacred. Believes in keeping your head down and never asking the Brenners for anything twice.
invariants: She would rather lose the job than let her son shame the family.
She hides pain until it changes her plans.

sample.reason: Invents Etta, her job, age, arthritis, clinic bill and family invariants.

card.identity: Commissioner of the city police department. Polished, patient, publicly paternal; privately willing to bury a case, a colleague or a witness to protect an arrangement that keeps his department funded and his name untouchable.

card.identity: A street dealer working the wet corners under the neon, thin as wire and patient as a priest. Sells the heroin that ends up in the narrator's pocket. Knows the city's supply lines and who owes whom; treats information as the only real currency. Has a personal history with the boss's organization that the narrator does not know about.
invariants: Sells the heroin the narrator carries
Withholds key information
Motivated by a debt of his own

sample.reason: Invents Marlowe, traits, debts and supplier history.

value.stance: Twelve years of oblique conflict with a woman Marguerite met exactly twice, and an unresolved hunger to understand why the garden was made this way.

card.identity: Director of the Civic Continuity Office, the soft-spoken architect of the memory erasure. She presents the erasure as mercy and public health, not tyranny, and she is not entirely wrong about what the outbreak did. Believes forgetting kept the city alive; will bargain before she will kill.

sample.reason: Invents Ilse and the Civic Continuity Office, motives and bargaining preference.

value.stance: The dreamer and the pragmatist, permanently arguing about what the city is for and quietly trusting no one else.

sample.reason: Adds Ray/Winston identities and dreamer/pragmatist relationship.

card.identity: The current president of Nijō Seika, sixty-two. Third-generation head of the confectionery house; calm, immaculate, and harder to read than his books. Deeply protective of the family name and punctilious about propriety. Believes the company is being attacked from outside and wants the matter handled quietly, before any auditor arrives in spring.
invariants: He refuses to consider publicly blaming a family member.
He speaks in complete, formal sentences even when cornered.

sample.reason: Invents Kaoru, age, company presidency and detailed family motives.

value.description: A four-lane highway bridge in a river town, summer of 1998, part of a fast-track municipal job. Concrete smells of lime and hot diesel, rebar laid out like a nervous system, and the whole structure hums when a loaded truck crosses it. Somewhere inside it is a number that is either right or not.

sample.reason: Invents Colfax Overpass, date, municipal job and sensory setting.

value.description: Cattle are penned in the barns from November to April on unbedded floors, so manure and urine compact into a heating pack that stays workable in subzero weather. In spring the cattle go to grass and pigs are turned in to root the pack for undigested corn, turning waste into pork at almost no feed cost. Produces cheap finished hogs, a stench that carries to town on south wind, and thin sick animals in the corners. The cycle depends on never removing the pack completely; feed-cost savings are the whole point.

sample.reason: Adds seasonal dates, unbedded floors, undigested corn and sick animals.

value.description: The prophecy thread: Nell yells 'the bench fell over' hours before the shore bench actually goes over, and the group spends the rest of the story trying to decide whether she saw the future or merely set a trap for the present. The bench does not go over before Nell's shout, and it does go over before the story ends.

sample.reason: Adds Nell and group speculation about a trap for the present.

value.stance: Two years together, ending on the night of Nadia's party. No betrayal, no single blow-up: they wore the relationship down by scheduling around it and calling that peace. After the breakup they stay dependent on each other in ordinary ways — texts about a broken chair, a lift to a dentist appointment — and the friendship survives because both keep choosing to show up rather than to be right.

sample.reason: Adds June/Theo, two years together, party host identity and reasons for breakup.

card.identity: Thirty-one, a physical therapist in her third year of private practice contract. Decisive in practical matters, slow in emotional ones; she spent the last year of the relationship cataloguing their problems in her head instead of saying them out loud. Ends things at the party because she can no longer pretend. Once things end, her honesty loosens.
invariants: She initiated the breakup at the party.
She speaks bluntly once she stops protecting the relationship.

sample.reason: Adds June age, profession, initiative and emotional traits.

value.description: Sera's life is being lived inside a sentence other people already know the end of. Each decision she makes is measured against it: her anger is proof, her calm is pretence, her kindness is a warning sign. The line is whether a name describes a life or commands one.

sample.reason: Adds Sera and concrete social interpretations of her behavior.

value.description: A dense dream forest with no moon and no dawn. Towering trees stand so close their crowns braid into a ceiling; the air is wet, warm, heavy with resin and crushed leaf. The light does not fall from above — it rises from plumes of low mist in a purple-green glow, so the undersides of leaves and the palms of Mara's hands are lit from below. Sound is muffled and delayed here, arriving a half-beat late, as if the forest were considering each noise before returning it.

sample.reason: Adds forest temperature, light mechanism, delayed sound and Mara.

value.stance: Uneasy partners bound by necessity: Mara does not trust an intelligence built by the same systems that erased her students, and Vell needs a mind that remembers. They cooperate while each keeps a reserve.

value.description: Six long white barns on the flat black ground north of Halder, six hundred head each, little ventilation, a concrete apron, and a manure pack that swells through winter. The barns smell of ammonia in cold weather and of rot in warm; the pack is never fully cleaned, only scraped where a machine must pass.

Interpretations are debated but the name itself is never contested.
